t: and upon the master. The lord.
home-born. Babies born to maidservants who belong to him.
and bought with money. Slaves he bought with his money.
for karet depends only on the uncircumcised person himself. Only if the uncircumcised person himself did not circumcise himself is he liable to karet, as explained in the next halakhah.
for the home-born is circumcised on the eighth. When he is eight days old, by the law of the commandment of circumcision, which applies also to slaves in an Israelite household (Genesis 17:12).
and the one bought with money is circumcised on the day he is bought. His circumcision is part of the process of making him from a gentile into a slave (Hilchot Issurei Biah 13:11).
bought a maidservant and bought her fetus with her. Bought a pregnant maidservant and together with her bought her fetus.
even though he bought the fetus by itself. For example, the maidservant belonged to one person and the fetus to another, and he bought each one's portion from each (Responsa of Maimonides, no. 164).
since he bought its mother before she gave birth, he is circumcised on the eighth. For when it was born its mother was in an Israelite's possession, and he has the law of a home-born.
bought a maidservant for her fetuses. Bought the right of ownership over the fetuses from the maidservant, but not the maidservant herself.

on condition not to immerse her for the sake of slavery. When buying a maidservant she must be immersed in order to leave the category of gentiles (see Hilchot Issurei Biah 13:11). But he may stipulate in advance not to immerse her.
and if its mother immersed after she gave birth. And thereby entered the category of Israelite maidservants (and see below halakhah 10).
they delay with him for a full twelve months. During this time they try to persuade him to be circumcised.

he stipulated regarding him at first while he was with his gentile master. The slave made a condition with the buyer while he belonged to the gentile master (see also Hilchot Issurei Biah 14:9; Hilchot Avadim 8:12).
that he accept upon himself seven commandments. The commandments that gentiles are obligated in (explained in Hilchot Melachim 9:1).

and he will be like a resident alien. Who accepts upon himself not to worship idolatry and to observe the other commandments of the children of Noah (see Hilchot Issurei Biah 14:7; Hilchot Melachim 8:10-11).

only when the Jubilee is in effect. That is when all the inhabitants of the land are on it, and each tribe dwells in its place. Since the exile of the two and a half tribes of Israel, the Jubilees have been nullified (Hilchot Shemitah VeYovel 10:8-9; and see also Hilchot Avodah Zarah 10:6; Hilchot Shabbat 20:14; Hilchot Issurei Biah 14:7).
a convert who entered the congregation of Israel. Who converts; the details of conversion are explained in Hilchot Issurei Biah chapters 13-14.
to draw from him a drop of the blood of the covenant when he converts. They draw a little blood from the circumcision site (see also Hilchot Issurei Biah 14:5).
who was born circumcised. Born without a foreskin.
one born by caesarean. A child delivered through the wall of the abdomen and not through the womb's opening (caesarean section).
and one who has two foreskins. One on top of the other, or who has two male organs.
on the eighth. But if the eighth day of any of these falls on the Sabbath, circumcision does not override the Sabbath (below halakhah 11).
after sunrise. The appearance of the sun, the beginning of sunrise.
the pillar of dawn. The beginning of the illumination of the east before sunrise (about an hour and a fifth before it, Commentary on the Mishnah, Berakhot 1:1).

and if he circumcised from when the pillar of dawn rose, it is valid. For this time too can be considered day (for further examples see Hilchot Keriat Shema 1:12; Hilchot Tefillah 3:7; Hilchot Parah 11:1).
the zealous hasten to commandments. For another example of this rule see Hilchot Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 4:6.
a bright spot. A kind of leprosy affliction (Hilchot Tumat Tzara'at 1:2).
for cutting off a leprous affliction is a negative commandment. Learned from the verse "Take heed in the plague of leprosy" (Deuteronomy 24:8; and see Hilchot Tumat Tzara'at 10:1).
let the positive commandment come. The commandment of circumcision.
and override the negative commandment. See also Hilchot Tumat Tzara'at 10:5 (for this principle see Hilchot Nezirut 7:15).
for even though he was circumcised on the eighth. Like a home-born (as explained above halakhah 5).
it does not override the Sabbath. For the obligation of his circumcision on the eighth day was not created at birth but as a result of the mother's immersion.
a child who was born circumcised. Who needs a drop of the blood of the covenant (as explained above halakhah 7; and see below 3:6).
before his formation was completed. His body did not develop properly.
like a stillborn because he is not viable. Born before his time and not destined to live (for the details of the law see below halakhot 13-15).
and one born by caesarean. His circumcision does not override the Sabbath, because overriding the Sabbath depends on the circumcision being on the eighth day from a complete birth.
and an androgynos. For his obligation of circumcision is not certain (below 3:6).
two foreskins. For it is uncertain which of them is the main one whose circumcision overrides the Sabbath.
twilight. The time of dusk, which is uncertain whether it belongs to the previous day or to the night of the next day. Its exact time is explained in Hilchot Shabbat 5:4.
we count from the night. It is better to circumcise a day late than before the time.

and if he was born Friday at twilight. It is uncertain whether he was born on Friday or on the Sabbath. By law the circumcision should be postponed to the Sabbath, but circumcision does not override the Sabbath on the basis of doubt, so he is circumcised on Sunday.

and he is a seven-month child but was delayed. According to the medicine of the Sages' time, some embryos need only seven months of pregnancy, and it is reasonable that this child, born in the eighth month, was already fit to be born but remained in his mother's womb an additional month.
and his hair is defective. Damaged, not grown properly.
regarded as a stone. This child is not defined as a living person, since he is destined to die, and is considered inanimate, neither alive nor dead (see Hilchot Tumat Met 1:14).
and it is forbidden to move him. Since it is forbidden to move on the Sabbath something that is not a vessel (see also Hilchot Shabbat 25:6, Hilchot Tumat Met 15:2).
for anyone who lived thirty days among people. Any child who lived thirty days is free of the concern of being a stillborn (see also Hilchot Evel 1:6-8; Hilchot Rotzeach 2:6).
if he was born complete. In his hair and nails, as explained in the previous halakhah.
this is a viable child. The signs indicate that he is a child who needs only seven months of pregnancy.
doubtful whether a seven-month or eight-month child. It is hard to tell from his hair and nails whether he is a child who needs seven months or a nine-month child born early (Yad Pashut).
in any case. According to each side of the doubt, as he goes on to explain.
we do not circumcise him on the Sabbath. For we go by the emergence of his head, which was at twilight, and he is circumcised on Sunday as explained above halakhah 12.
and it overrides the second day of the festival. Of the Diaspora, which is observed only because of a custom from the Sages' words (Hilchot Yom Tov 1:21, 6:14, Hilchot Kiddush HaChodesh 5:6).
and on the two festival days of Rosh Hashanah. For the two days of Rosh Hashanah are considered one sanctity and one long day (Hilchot Yom Tov 1:24).
from the time he recovers from his illness. From the time he is healed of his illness.
seven days, from time to time. Seven complete days of twenty-four hours.
when a fever seized him. His body temperature rose.
and the like of this illness. An illness affecting his entire body.
very green. That is, pale yellow, like the appearance of jaundice.
until blood falls into it. Until the flow of blood returns to normal.
until his blood is absorbed in it. Until the blood is absorbed in the limbs.
that has no name of illness. That he is not sick at all.
with a flint. A sharp stone.
with a reed splinter. The hard peel of a reed that has been sharpened and can serve as a knife.
because of the danger. Lest a splinter of wood wound the baby.
the covering. The covering.
the crown. The head of the organ.
they tear. They tear the membrane to expose the flesh.
the soft membrane. Beneath the foreskin there is another thin layer of skin.
and turns it this way and that. He pulls the membrane to the sides so that the flesh is exposed.
they remove him. They dismiss him from serving as mohel.
a plaster or a bandage. Dressings spread with ointment for healing.
shreds. Pieces of skin that remained and were not cut with the foreskin.
they prevent the circumcision. Their cutting is essential, and if he did not cut them he has not fulfilled the commandment of circumcision.
he returns. And fixes the shreds.
finished. Finished circumcising.
as if he had not circumcised. And has not fulfilled the commandment.
soft and hanging. Flaccid, and appearing as if his organ is covered with a foreskin.
fleshy. Fat.
at the time he becomes erect. When the organ is erect and its flesh is stretched.
and he must fix the flesh on this side and that. To push it backward so that he will not look uncircumcised.
preparations for circumcision. The preparations required for performing the circumcision, which can also be done from Friday.
and we do not bring it from place to place. Because of the prohibition of carrying an object from one domain to another (Hilchot Shabbat 12:8 ff.).
in an alley. A lane into which several courtyards with houses open.

that has no eruv etc.. By Torah law one may carry from courtyard to courtyard through the alley, but by rabbinic law all who live in the alley must combine their dwellings in an eruv (Hilchot Eruvin 1:1-2).
the eruv of their words. The law of the eruv, although it is rabbinic.
this is the rule. This rule is detailed in Hilchot Shabbat 6:9-10.
we do not grind spices for it. For the healing of the baby after circumcision.
and we do not make a bandage for it. For making it involves the prohibition of smearing (Hilchot Shabbat 11:6).

and we do not mix wine and oil. We do not mix wine and oil into a mixture used as an ointment for the circumcision site, which is among the healing actions forbidden on the Sabbath out of a decree lest he grind spices (Hilchot Shabbat 21:20).
cumin. Cumin.
chews with his teeth. Which differs from the usual way of grinding (and likewise in applying the wine and oil separately).

on the third day of circumcision. For on the third day there is danger to the circumcised, as stated (Genesis 34:25): "And it was on the third day, when they were in pain" (Commentary on the Mishnah, Shabbat 19:3).

whether with hot water that was heated on Friday or with hot water that they heat for him on the Sabbath. For example, if the hot water spilled, or on the third day of his circumcision if they did not heat in advance. But on the day of the circumcision, if they did not heat water from Friday, the circumcision is postponed to the ninth day, as explained in the previous halakhah (Responsa of Maimonides, no. 307; and see also Hilchot Shabbat 2:14).
provided that he does not bring it by way of the public domain. For such carrying is forbidden by Torah law.
because of a shevut. By decree of the Sages, and not a labor prohibited by the Torah.
it is permitted for us to tell a gentile to do it in order to perform a commandment. As explained in Hilchot Shabbat 6:9-10.

since they are fit for the pot. And it is permitted on a festival to grind them to prepare food (Hilchot Yom Tov 1:8), and since this is so, the matter is permitted also for the purpose of circumcision.

circumcised his fellow's son... circumcised his own son. When one fulfills the commandment for his own son, which is the complete way of performing the commandment, the wording of the blessing is "to circumcise". When he fulfills it for another, the wording is "on the circumcision" (and likewise in other blessings such as below halakhah 5; for the detail of the rule see Hilchot Berakhot 11:11-13; Responsa of Maimonides, no. 32).
for it is a commandment upon the father to circumcise his sons. Therefore he recites an additional blessing over the commandment.
those standing. Other people present.
"Blessed are You" etc.. A blessing that deals, in poetic language, with the sanctity of the people of Israel, the covenant made between it and the Holy One, blessed be He, and a prayer for salvation.

He sanctified the beloved from the womb. He sanctified Abraham our father, who is called the friend of the Holy One, blessed be He, from his mother's womb (Tosafot); some explain it as Isaac our father (Rashi), or Jacob our father (Geonim).
and He set a statute in his flesh. He commanded him the circumcision engraved in the flesh.

therefore, as reward for this, the living God, our portion, ordained forever. As reward for the commandment of circumcision, the Holy One, blessed be He, became our portion forever by making an eternal covenant with us (see Genesis 17:7; Responsa of Maimonides, no. 214).
command as You commanded to the holy ones. Command as You commanded our holy fathers.
to save the beloved of our flesh from destruction. To save the lives of the remnant of Your people from ruin.
and the father of the son recites "who has kept us alive". And see also Hilchot Berakhot 11:9.
for were it not for the blood of the covenant, heaven and earth would not endure. The world endures by virtue of the observance of the commandment of circumcision.
must cover his nakedness. For one may not say words of holiness facing nakedness (see Hilchot Keriat Shema 3:16).
when they draw from them a drop of the blood of the covenant. As explained above 1:7.
because it is not certain. For it is doubtful whether she is female.
we do not lift them out of the hands of death. We do not save them when they are in danger (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 10:1-2, Hilchot Rotzeach 4:11).
that he has made a commandment. He removes the foreskin, and thereby there is fulfillment of a commandment (see Hilchot Melachim 10:10; Responsa of Maimonides, no. 148).
and left his foreskin. Left his foreskin and did not remove it.
or pulled it. Covered it with his flesh so that it would not be evident that he is circumcised.
for he was not given a reprieve. He was not given an extension to fulfill it, when he was on the way from Midian to Egypt and did not circumcise his son (Exodus 4:24-26).
only three covenants were made over them. The word "covenant" is mentioned three times in relation to the commandments of the Torah as a whole.
